item.title: Trouser Press Turns 50 | Trouser Press
item.description: Saturday, March 16th, Trouser Press will celebrate its 50th birthday – and launch Zip It Up! The Best of Trouser Press Magazine 1974-1984 – with a gala party at Bowery Electric in New York. Trouser Press co-founder Ira Robbins will host.

item.description: Living in San Francisco in the late 1970s, Philip Polarov is a writer scraping by on a series of odd jobs while attempting to turn his self-described "stream of drivel" into an Important Novel. item.title: Never Understood So Well: The Jesus and Mary Chain | Trouser Press
item.description: The effect is not of a book being read aloud, but of two enormously likable fellows alternately recounting their shared life story for nine mesmerizing hours. It’s weirdly intimate, almost as if they’re speaking directly to you. And with colorful inflections. It’s fucking brilliant.

item.title: Art Fein: Rock's in My Head | Trouser Press
item.description: In 2022, Trouser Press Books published Rock's in My Head, a memoir by the fabled LA scenester Art Fein, based on 10,000 pages of journals he had kept. Art died July 30, following surgery for a broken hip. He was 79.

item.title: Book Bit: Graham Parker's Howlin' Wind | Trouser Press
item.description: In his new book, Graham Parker’s Howlin' Wind, author Jay Nachman tells the story of making that acclaimed 1976 album, using interviews with Parker, Nick Lowe, all of the members of the Rumour, manager Dave Robinson and others.
